examples.solution_text:
The tangent is perpendicular to the radius, so $\angle OTP=90^{\circ}$.

$\begin{align*}x+90^{\circ}+63^{\circ}&=180^{\circ}\\x&=27^{\circ}\end{align*}$

(a) Tangents meet radii at right angles: $\angle OTP=\angle OQP=90^{\circ}$.

$\begin{align*}\angle TPQ+90^{\circ}+90^{\circ}+120^{\circ}&=360^{\circ}\\\angle TPQ&=60^{\circ}\end{align*}$

(b) $PT=PQ$ because tangents from the same external point are equal. Triangle $TPQ$ is isosceles.

$\begin{align*}\angle PTQ&=\frac{180^{\circ}-60^{\circ}}{2}\\\angle PTQ&=60^{\circ}\end{align*}$

(c) The tangent $PT$ and chord $TQ$ give $\angle TCQ=\angle PTQ=60^{\circ}$ by the alternate segment theorem.

(a) $\angle TAB=70^{\circ}$ by the alternate segment theorem for chord $TB$.

(b) Use the angle sum of triangle $ATB$.

$\begin{align*}\angle ABT&=180^{\circ}-45^{\circ}-70^{\circ}\\\angle ABT&=65^{\circ}\end{align*}$

(c) $\angle XTA=\angle ABT=65^{\circ}$ by the alternate segment theorem for chord $TA$.

(a) First find the full secant length: $PB=PN+NB=2+6=8\text{ cm}$.

The square of a tangent equals the external segment multiplied by the full secant length.

$\begin{align*}PC^{2}&=PN\times PB\\PC^{2}&=2\times8\\PC^{2}&=16\\PC&=4\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

(b) Equal tangents from $P$ give $PQ=PC=4\text{ cm}$.

(c) $\angle OCP=90^{\circ}$ because a tangent is perpendicular to the radius. Use Pythagoras' theorem in triangle $OCP$.

$\begin{align*}OP^{2}&=OC^{2}+PC^{2}\\5^{2}&=OC^{2}+4^{2}\\OC^{2}&=25-16\\OC^{2}&=9\\OC&=3\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

(d) $y\approx26.57^{\circ}$ by the alternate segment theorem for chord $CN$.

Apply the tangent-secant product rule to find the full length $PB$.

$\begin{align*}PC^{2}&=PN\times PB\\14^{2}&=7\times PB\\196&=7\times PB\\PB&=28\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

Subtract the external segment.

$\begin{align*}NB&=PB-PN\\NB&=28-7\\NB&=21\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

The full secant length is $PB=PN+NB=5+9=14\text{ cm}$.

$\begin{align*}PC^{2}&=PN\times PB\\PC^{2}&=5\times14\\PC^{2}&=70\\PC&=\sqrt{70}\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

(a) $PT=PQ$ because tangents from the same external point are equal. Triangle $TPQ$ is isosceles.

$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{180^{\circ}-48^{\circ}}{2}\\x&=66^{\circ}\end{align*}$

(b) Apply the tangent-secant product rule.

$\begin{align*}PT^{2}&=PA\times PB\\15^{2}&=10\times PB\\225&=10\times PB\\PB&=22.5\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

(a) In triangles $PAO$ and $PBO$:

$\angle PAO=\angle PBO=90^{\circ}$ because tangents meet radii at right angles.

$OA=OB$ because both are radii.

$OP$ is the common hypotenuse.

Therefore $\triangle PAO\equiv\triangle PBO$ by RHS.

(b) $PA=PB$ because corresponding sides of congruent triangles are equal.

examples.derivation: OT is perpendicular to PT. The triangle angle sum gives x = 180° − 90° − 63° = 27°. The coordinates give angle TOP approximately 63°.

The two tangent-radius angles are 90°, so angle TPQ = 360° − 180° − 120° = 60°. Equal tangents give angle PTQ = (180° − 60°)/2 = 60°. The alternate segment theorem gives angle TCQ = 60°. Both contact radii are perpendicular to their tangents, and C lies in the required alternate segment.

The alternate segment theorem gives angle TAB = 70°. Then angle ABT = 180° − 45° − 70° = 65°, and angle XTA = 65°. The repaired A coordinate lies on the radius-2 circle; TA and TB have directions approximately 115° and 70°, giving the stated 45° angle at T.

PB=2+6=8 cm. The tangent-secant rule gives PC²=2×8=16, so PC=4 cm. Equal tangents give PQ=4 cm. The tangent-radius right triangle gives OC²=5²−4²=9, so OC=3 cm. The alternate segment theorem gives y≈26.57°. The coordinates independently give radius 3, OP=5, PC=4 and ∠NCP≈26.565°. The relocated O and NB labels preserve the givens without revealing answers.
14² = 7 × PB gives PB = 28 cm. Thus NB = 28 − 7 = 21 cm. Coordinate lengths PN = 1.4, NB = 4.2 and PC = 2.8 share the same scale, and OC is perpendicular to PC.
PB = 5 + 9 = 14 cm. PC² = 5 × 14 = 70, so PC = √70 cm. The coordinates place C on the circle and make PC perpendicular to its radius; the secant segment ratio is 5:9.

Equal tangents make triangle TPQ isosceles, so x=(180°−48°)/2=66°. The tangent-secant rule gives 15²=10×PB, hence PB=22.5 cm. The coordinates place A and B on the circle in the stated order, with PB/PA≈2.25. The arc spans the full 48° angle between PT and PQ, and its label leader terminates on that arc.

Angles PAO and PBO are both 90°. OA = OB as radii, and OP is the common hypotenuse, so triangles PAO and PBO are congruent by RHS. Corresponding sides give PA = PB. The diagram has both contact points on the circle and both tangents perpendicular to their radii.
